source_excerpts.text:
## 9. The perturbation norm and bounded spectators matter

The uniform statement controls the **total operator norm** of W_N. A bound on every individual pair term is insufficient when the number of terms touching a unit can grow.

A simple counterexample uses local two-level Hamiltonians \(h_i=\delta|1\rangle\langle1|_i\), with target all zeros. Define

\[
W_N=-\eta\sum_{j=2}^N
|1\rangle\langle1|_1\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|_j.
\]

Each spectator term has norm eta and preserves every diagonal local symmetry. The state with only unit 1 excited has energy \(\delta-\eta(N-1)\). Choosing \(\eta=\delta/(N-1)\) closes the gap even though every individual coupling tends to zero as N grows. This is a gap counterexample, not a decay claim. Uniform bounds at fixed interaction strength per edge require further assumptions such as bounded coordination and an applicable many-body stability theorem; neither is established here.

A scalar spectator shift \(c_N I\) leaves the gap unchanged. A general additional spectator operator of total norm d changes the elementary guaranteed gap by at most 2d and must be counted in the same perturbation budget. Merely calling each spectator contribution bounded does not provide an N-independent budget.

## D. Tensor-sum gap: correct target,access and perturbation budget

Let E be a simple isolated eigenvalue on the actual reducing sector K,with
projection P and nonempty complement spectrum S=sigma((H-E)|_(I-P)K),distance
delta>0 from0. Splitting each tensor factor into P and I-P shows that the
complement spectrum for N copies is the closure of all nonempty sums of at
most N elements of S. If S is one-sided,the distance is exactly delta for
every N: sums cannot cancel,and one non-target factor realizes the old edge.
If a<0<b lie in S,rational b/|a| gives exact integer cancellation; irrational
ratio gives arbitrarily small sums by rational approximation. Adding target
spectators preserves previous spectral values,so the distances decrease to0.
This proves the stated iff criterion,not a statement about an energy value
whose target multiplicity is allowed to grow.

For a negative point a and a positive interval [u-w,u+w],u>w>0,choose n with
n w>|a|/2 and k nearest n u/|a|. Then k>=1 and
k a+n[u-w,u+w] contains0 in its interior. Spectral tensor products give
essential spectrum at some finite N and every larger N. Interchanging signs
covers the reverse case. No radiation matrix element follows from overlap.

A total perturbation norm v<delta/2 retains a rank-one Riesz projection and
gap at least delta-2v. A per-edge bound does not supply that budget: with
h_i=delta |1><1| and W=-eta sum_(j>1) |1><1|_1 tensor |0><0|_j,the one-excited
state has energy delta-eta(N-1). At eta=delta/(N-1),each edge tends to zero but
the target loses its gap. The converse's rank-two counterperturbation can be
N-body and nonlocal; it is not a theorem that every local coupler causes decay.
One vector's spectral measure is not a substitute for a common reducing space
invariant under all allowed interactions.
